title: Coral Reefs
objective: After this level you can explain why coral reefs hold so much life.
summary: Reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean but house nearly a quarter of its species. Polyps build the city, and algae in their tissues feed it with sunlight.

cards.headline: Less than 1% of the ocean. Nearly a quarter of its species.
cards.body: Coral reefs are specks on a map of the sea, yet they are packed like nowhere else. Why would so much life crowd into so little space? The answer is a building, a lodger and a lot of sunshine.

cards.headline: A city built by animals
cards.body: A reef is built by coral polyps, tiny soft animals that each lay down a hard limestone skeleton. Hundreds to thousands of them make one coral, and corals together make a reef full of ledges, holes and hideouts. Fish, crabs and sea turtles use it to feed, shelter and raise their young. NOAA calls reefs the rainforests of the sea. On a reef, the scenery is also the housing.

cards.headline: The lodger that pays the rent
cards.body: Living inside the coral's tissues are microscopic algae. The coral gives them shelter, plus the carbon dioxide and water they need for photosynthesis. In return, as much as 90% of the food the algae make passes to the coral. It's one of the best rental deals in nature: the tenant pays in food, and the landlord builds a whole city on it.
cards.callout: Coral: shelter · Algae: up to 90% of their food

cards.headline: Why reefs need clear, sunny water
cards.body: Here's the catch. The lodgers run on sunlight, so reef-building corals thrive in clear, warm, moving tropical water where light reaches their algae. Remember Level 8: light fades with depth, and below about 200 m there's too little for photosynthesis. Like the kelp of Level 42, which rarely grows deeper than about 15 to 40 m, reef builders are solar-powered. For them, murky water is a power cut.

cards.headline: Coral reefs: explained
learned: Under 1% of the ocean, nearly a quarter of its species
Polyps build a city of hideouts and nurseries
Algae in the coral pay rent in food
Reef builders need clear, sunlit water

questions.prompt: Coral reefs occur in less than 1% of the ocean. About what share of all ocean species live on them?

options.label: About three quarters
options.rationale: Too high: it's nearly a quarter.

questions.explanation: Reefs occur in less than 1% of the ocean, yet NOAA says they are home to nearly a quarter of all ocean species.

questions.prompt: What do the algae living inside reef corals give the coral?

options.label: Most of the food they make by photosynthesis
Protection from reef fish
options.rationale: The coral shelters the algae, not the reverse.

options.label: Fresh water to drink
options.rationale: The coral gives the algae water, not the reverse.

questions.explanation: As much as 90% of the food the algae make passes to the coral; the coral gives them shelter, carbon dioxide and water.

questions.prompt: From Level 8: why do reef-building corals need clear, shallow water?

options.label: Their skeletons dissolve in deep water
options.rationale: This level is about light, not skeletons.

options.label: Polyps must breathe air at low tide
Reef fish can't swim below 30 m
options.rationale: The limit comes from the coral's algae.

options.label: Their algae need sunlight to make food

questions.explanation: Light fades with depth, and the coral's algae need it for photosynthesis, so reef builders stay in clear, sunlit water.
